issue.title: Implement transport circuit breaking in aggregator

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
This commit moves the action name validation and circuit breaking into
the InboundAggregator. This work is valuable because it lays the 
groundwork for incrementally circuit breaking as data is received.

This PR includes the follow behavioral change:

Handshakes contribute to circuit breaking, but cannot be broken. They
currently do not contribute nor are they broken.

body:
I just came across this exact problem when trying to upgrade a 9-node cluster from 6.8.4 to 7.6.2

> fatal error in thread [Thread-5616], exiting java.lang.AssertionError: illegal transport ID from node of version: 5.6.0 got

Is there a work around for this problem whilst waiting for a proper fix ?

@baileygm do you see this happening consistently or was it a one-off? I think the only workaround today is to carry on with the upgrade. In particular if the 6.8 node has shut down then you can upgrade it to 7.6 and restart it.
Unfortunately I think everything in the OP about 7.6 nodes is also true of 7.0 nodes so it doesn't help to do this upgrade in multiple steps.

issue.title: Close channel on handshake error with old version

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Today a transport response uses the same wire format version as the
corresponding request. This mostly works since we mostly know we are
communicating with a node with a compatible version. TCP handshakes don't have
this guarantee since they use `Version.CURRENT.minimumCompatibilityVersion()`
to let us handshake with older nodes. This results in the strange situation of
a node of major version `N` responding to a node of major version `N-1` using a
wire format of version `N-2`.

We put extra effort into the longer BWC requirements for successful responses,
but we do not offer the same guarantees for error responses since they may be
rather complicated to serialize. This can result in the request sender misinterpreting
the response which may have unpredictable consequences.

Rather than strengthening the guarantees in this area, this commit simply logs
the exception and closes the connection on a handshake error with a node that
uses an incompatible wire format.

Closes #54337
